# Original qmatch source and evidence coupling

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz) and [index](index.json) preserve original
sources, actual diagnostics, separate repairs, exact source/import byte maps
and observers as text. The archive includes the preceding finite/Raw/nominal
sector and quantum-header studies; it neither extracts nor executes history.
The index binds every complete member, and the archive was read back to verify
all sizes and hashes without execution. Final current checks are recorded
separately in [validation](validation.json).

The first `SourceSector` prototype accepts a changed original arm function
while retaining free implementation indices. Its failed runtime assertion is
a real counterexample in an unexposed component. The repair proposes actual
function-evidence indices, derives implementation programs from those entries
and includes the evidence subjects in one fresh graph. Original resolved names,
source bytes, complete inputs, actual dependency snapshots and exact main/U/CU
equations remain bound together. Changing a resolved function cannot retain
the same evidence table and index under the generic checked binding theorem.

Twenty-two small runtime observations include correct canonical phase order,
an independent valid schedule and rejection of source/entry/body/phase/control
substitutions, missing evidence, unused graph nodes and unused source rows.
Two actual controlled/main phase mutations reach the exact equation refusal;
changes leaving an unrelated node instead fail graph coverage. These are runtime
observations, separately from the generic kernel-checked composition theorems
and four small original-identity reductions.

The first full-computation kernel examples hit the existing recursion depth;
a diagnostic reduction also reaches the existing heartbeat limit. Those failed
attempts stay unchanged. The limits are not raised, and the failed examples
are not presented as proofs. Shared generic fresh-receipt/input/source coupling
proofs avoid repeated whole-source evaluation. The smaller identity reductions
retain their stated scope; they do not prove concrete complete source execution.

Other retained failures include absent import products in early observer runs,
reserved identifiers, missing equality instances, incorrect offsets, proof
elaboration and unused-simplification warnings. They remain failed observations.
Primary import products are hash-bound, not freshly replayed by these component
checks. No native mode, source execution handle, QDV route, whole-source body
preservation, external schema, new guarantee or Issue completion is established.
Selector/target expression typing, general/selected quantum nominal execution,
the twelve-bit qmatch profile and #64/#195 remain unfinished. The two protected
QLV1 scopes and all pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations remain unchanged.

The separate [operand history](operands-first.tar.xz),
[index](operands-index.json) and [current checks](operands-validation.json)
retain seven source-name/frame counterexamples, the equal-type zero-width owner
substitution and the public Observe sharpening counterexample. All arise in
unexposed components. Correct direct and tuple-aliased sources stay separate
from malformed sources; the escaped local name reaches an unsupported-prefix
barrier and is not evidence of general block-scope checking.

Original structural parameter/move checking repairs those cases. The first
compiled audit rejects a generated partial recursive helper; a library-fold
repair and exact `take_cons`/declarative `Move` proofs preserve the name-transfer
rule. Twelve small kernel reductions cover zero-width moves, grouping versus
singleton tuples, atomic quantum product owners, wildcard/duplicate/consumed
names and simultaneous tuple bindings. Thirty-four runtime observations retain
separate scopes from the generic proofs and complete kernel Tests.
Arbitrary calls, allocation, control flow, full source-to-Raw mapping and native
execution remain unfinished; no component or barrier closes #64/#195.

The [transport history](transport-first.tar.xz), [index](transport-index.json)
and [current validation](transport-validation.json) retain the first named-arm
request, original Unit-owner source, graph packet and 112 inert records. The
old executable's first observation is a legacy IO/artifact error: it did not
implement the proposed mode, and that input was request JSON rather than a
QLV3 packet. It is not a semantic qmatch refusal or an explicit unknown-mode error.

The first complete request check fails because the ordinary proposed order
omits separate arm subjects. A complete-order adapter repairs the proposal;
independent original-source checking still derives roots and rejects unrelated
nodes. The shared 33-case reader study then finds the real port-width mismatch:
Lean accepts 256 where Rust's u8 storage refuses. The separate repair aligns
the shared codec. Private/generated declarations retain the existing audit.

Other first failures include proof elaboration, unavailable JSON constructors,
a forbidden pure-kernel import of a transport test, observer path restrictions
and IO/error-helper mistakes. Their original sources and actual diagnostic
streams remain separate from repairs; tool-only observer failures are identified
as transcriptions, without inventing missing full streams. Two accepted exact
scalar controls and 24 original-source/body/evidence/QDV refusals use independently
authored literal expectations. These run the actual pure QLV3 definitions and
do not establish Rust retained-view integration, native-mode dispatch, source
body lowering, ordinary/selected quantum execution or Issue completion.

The [native-binding first history](native-binding-first.tar.xz),
[index](native-binding-index.json) and [local validation](native-binding-validation.json)
retain 167 records of actual Rust retained-graph/QDV materialization and paired
context dispatch. The first build misses three private ordinary-test adapter
arguments; all original source objects and compiler diagnostics remain separate
from the repair. The ordinary single-root check still rejects the same detached
subjects; the qmatch proposal derives roots only from actual requested entries
and controlled programs. Fresh Lean source relevance remains mandatory.

Normal/MSRV observations each pass three retained-data tests and leave two
fresh-native tests explicitly unexecuted. Independent exact phase expectations
cover the actual circuit/matrix caches, not a JSON replay. Pure context dispatch
checks the actual product/mode/scope/request and remaining work. These observations
are not fresh compiled-native acceptance, full CI or a source-body theorem.
The component has no public ordinary-program conversion or inverse/control
access. Canonical hosted proof maintenance, actual native execution, complete
ordinary/selected source integration and #64/#195 remain unfinished.

The [first hosted build](ci-typecheck-first.tar.xz),
[index](ci-typecheck-index.json) and [separate repair](ci-typecheck-validation.json)
retain the actual failed kernel compiler streams at commit `c6615d53` and both
versions of `Coordinates.lean`. Strict package compilation rejects undeclared
type parameters with `autoImplicit = false`; the later `sorry` diagnostics are
elaboration failures in that rejected build, not accepted project axioms.
Explicit independent type parameters repair the declaration without changing
proof limits or package options. All 98 changed modules and transitive local
dependents then compile afresh using bound unchanged imports. Earlier local
root checks reused import products and did not establish that full recompilation.
The technical inventory records the bounded component and its remaining gaps.
Canonical both-package proof maintenance, native execution and required CI
remain separate from these component observations; neither Issue is closed.

The [nominal first history](nominal-first.tar.xz), [index](nominal-index.json)
and [current checks](nominal-validation.json) retain informed three/four-label
sources and independently authored exact phase/QDV expectations. Their two-bit
selectors retain a distinct zero-width Unit target and reordered written arms.
The first physical diagonal proposal acts on selector axes and meets the
component's explicit unsupported-step barrier. A separately proposed controlled
scalar decomposition preserves the same intended diagonal action.

The first four-label QDV oracle incorrectly uses a zeta-power coordinate for
the eighth-root scalar. Its actual `decodedView` refusal is retained. The
separate repair follows the specified `a+b sqrt(2)+i(c+d sqrt(2))` coordinates:
both radical coefficients are one half. This is an oracle correction, not a
relaxation of the native comparison. All first compiler streams and source
objects remain inert; tool-only observer setup failures are transcriptions.

Current pure context checks and normal/MSRV retained-data tests cover four
positive controls in total and the 24 new nominal refusals. Ten reach exact
equation failure, twelve request failure and two stale-view failure; a work
limit or an earlier parser barrier cannot replace those expected stages.
Two conditional compiled-native Rust tests remain unexecuted locally. This
does not establish ordinary project/selected quantum execution, a source-body
preservation theorem, the full twelve-bit profile or Issue completion.
